# Hero block - integration notes

This is the scroll-driven 3D hero for the Data Center Valley site. A 2U node gets assembled from parts, powers on, slides into a rack, the rack turns into a row and the row into a full data hall. Then the building closes over the hall, the camera pulls back over the campus and climbs to orbit, where routes from the hub in Kazakhstan are drawn on a globe.

It is rendered live with three.js (0.170), GSAP ScrollTrigger and the postprocessing library, built with Vite. There are no model or texture files, everything is generated in code. The only data file is the country outlines (Natural Earth, public domain, about 67 KB gzipped).

## Running it

```
npm install
npm run dev       # http://localhost:5180
npm run build     # output goes to dist/
npm run preview
```

Handy URL parameters when reviewing:

- `?p=0.62` jumps to a point in the story. The range is 0 to 1.5, where 0 to 1 is node to hall and 1 to 1.5 is campus and globe
- `?debug=1` shows draw calls, triangles, quality tier, dpr and GPU time
- `?tier=0..3` locks the quality tier, 0 is the highest

## Adding the block to a page

The whole block is one `<section class="dcv-hero">`. You can find it in `index.html` between the HERO BLOCK comments. Copy that markup into your page and include the built files from `dist/assets`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/index-XXXX.css" />
<script type="module" src="/assets/index-XXXX.js"></script>
```

On load the script looks for `.dcv-hero` sections and mounts the scene into each one. Nothing else to call.

What is inside the section:

- `.dcv-pin` is pinned while the story plays, for 780% of the viewport height. The page scrolls normally before and after it
- `.dcv-visual` is the panel with the canvas. The canvas always stays inside this panel, it never goes fullscreen or fixed
- `[data-stage-index]`, `[data-stage-label]`, `[data-stage-title]` are the caption, `[data-progress]` is the progress line, `[data-sound]` is the sound toggle
- `.dcv-footer` is normal content after the pinned part

A few things to know:

- GSAP and ScrollTrigger are bundled in. If your site already uses GSAP and you want a single copy, build from source and mark gsap as external in the Vite config.
- Smooth scroll libraries (Lenis, Locomotive) work through the usual `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy` setup.
- Fonts are Inter, Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono with system fallbacks. The block doesn't load them, it expects them on the page.
- The scene mounts once when the script loads and there is no teardown yet. That is fine for a regular page. For a SPA with client-side routing you would import `mountHero` from `src/main.js` and call it yourself when the section appears, and we would need to add a destroy method. Tell us if you need that.
- Stage captions are in `src/config.js`, the callout labels in `src/scene/labels.js`, the page copy in `index.html`.
- All numbers in the scene are placeholders (10 kW per node, 200 kW per rack, 89 racks and 18 MW per row, 3,000 racks per hall, seven buildings). Please replace them with real ones.
- Hub location, cities, routes, latency values and highlighted countries are in `src/config.js` (`HUB`, `CITIES`, `ROUTES`, `MAP_LABELS`, `HIGHLIGHT`). Label styles are `.dcv-city`, `.dcv-ms`, `.dcv-hubtag` and `.dcv-note` in `src/styles.css`.

## Source layout

- `src/scene/world.js` builds the scene and holds all the animation. Everything is computed from scroll progress, so scrolling back works the same as forward
- `src/scene/camera.js` camera keyframes, the climb over the campus and the flight to orbit
- `src/scene/server.js`, `rack.js`, `datacenter.js` the node, the rack and the hall (the hall is one instanced mesh with about 3,000 racks)
- `src/scene/site.js` buildings, rooftop chillers, substation, power line, ground with roads
- `src/scene/globe.js`, `maplabels.js`, `src/util/earth.js` the globe, routes and city labels
- `src/scene/floor.js` reflective floor
- `src/scene/lights.js`, `materials.js`, `src/util/textures.js` lighting, materials, procedural textures
- `src/scene/post.js` bloom, tone mapping, antialiasing
- `src/scene/quality.js` adaptive quality
- `src/audio.js` synthesized sound, off by default
- `src/styles.css` all styles, every class is prefixed with `dcv-`
- `src/data/world.js` country outlines, generated by `tools/build-world.mjs`

## Performance

Measured on an M4 Pro at dpr 2 in a 1500x1000 window: 3 to 8 ms of GPU time per frame depending on the stage, CPU stays under 2 ms. The heaviest parts are the node close-up and the row (about 1.2M triangles). Campus and globe are lighter than the hall.

Quality adapts to the measured frame rate in four tiers (device pixel ratio, floor reflection, bloom, length of the detailed row). Phones start in a lighter mode with simpler materials and one set of lights. Rendering stops while the block is off screen.

Safari compiles shaders synchronously, so on load the scene warms them up in small chunks and shows the progress in the loader.

## Fallbacks and browsers

WebGL2 is required. Without it the block shows a static panel instead of the scene. With `prefers-reduced-motion` the parallax and idle motion are turned off. Devices that can't render to half-float buffers fall back to 8 bit.

Works in current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari 16+, desktop and mobile.
